title: Fourier coefficient after coordinate projection
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For a subset $J$ of the $n$ coordinates, define the coordinate projection by fixing the coordinates in $J$ and averaging over an independent product sample from $\pi$ in the other coordinates. For a function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ and multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of this projection at $a$ equals the coefficient of $f$ at $a$ if every coordinate where $a$ differs from the constant index belongs to $J$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
The basis is indexed by $\iota$ and spans the real-valued functions on $\Omega$
The basis vector at the distinguished index is constant $1$
$J$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
